title: Tencent releases Hy4 flash for lower-cost hosted workloads
dek: Tencent’s smaller Hy4 tier reaches hosted services, while Vercel offers a separate introductory discount with a different end date.
lede: Tencent released Hy4 flash on November 16 as a lower-cost model for everyday work. Vercel added the model to AI Gateway the same day, giving developers another hosted route into the new tier.

body.heading: A cheaper tier reaches users
body.text: Tencent positions Flash around routine document work and research, reserving the larger Hy4 for more demanding software projects. The company reports a one-million-token context window and multimodal input. WorkBuddy access is free through November 30, alongside a half-price TokenHub promotion. These are temporary offers attached to particular services. The standard token rates provide the more useful starting point for a budget that extends beyond this month.

body.heading: The gateway has its own controls
body.text: Vercel’s announcement lists image input, tool calling, structured output and prompt caching. Its integration preserves thinking between turns and permits requests with reasoning disabled. Developers select tencent/hy4-flash through AI Gateway; the introductory discount covers input, cached input and output tokens. That creates a practical distinction between choosing a model and choosing a route to it. A team using a gateway can keep that integration boundary while changing the model underneath. Whether a particular application benefits depends on the requests it actually sends.

body.heading: The larger model remains the reference point
body.text: Tencent’s November 4 Hy4 announcement priced ordinary input at about $0.90 per million tokens and output at $2.70. It also described visual understanding, computer use through graphical and command-line interfaces, and training involving Blender and CAD. That release concentrated on broadening the kinds of work the family could perform. Flash now adds a cheaper hosted option to the same purchasing decision. The distinction matters for routing: an application can separate routine transformations from work that needs a longer sequence of decisions, without treating every request as the same purchase.

body.heading: Token prices are only one part of the result
body.text: Consider a hypothetical assistant that turns a customer brief into a structured project plan. One attempt might return valid fields immediately; another might require a repair request after producing an invalid date. Both initial answers could look plausible in a demonstration. Their useful outputs differ once the application checks the result. The relevant comparison includes the original request, any repair attempts and the final accepted plan. A low-priced answer that repeatedly needs correction can consume more reviewer time than its token bill suggests. This is an evaluation example, not a result measured for Flash.

body.heading: Discounts set a test window
body.text: The two promotion deadlines create a short period for trials, not a permanent production price. A useful comparison separates model behavior from procurement: identical source material and acceptance rules establish the first, while the selected endpoint and normal tariff establish the second. For the project-plan example, a pass could require preserved deadlines, valid owner fields and no invented commitments. Those criteria make a cheaper model’s result comparable with an existing workflow instead of rewarding the most polished first draft.

buildersNote: Replay 20 non-sensitive, previously completed tasks through the candidate route. Record accepted results, repair attempts and reviewer minutes. Compare normal-rate costs separately from the introductory bill, using the same acceptance criteria for the incumbent model.

social.hook: A cheaper model still has to finish the job.
social.voiceover: [matter-of-fact] A cheaper model still has to finish the job. Tencent released Hy four flash. Vercel’s half-price offer runs through November twenty-ninth. [measured] Compare accepted results, including repairs, before changing production traffic.
social.short: Tencent released Hy4 flash for lower-cost hosted work. Vercel added it to AI Gateway with half-price tokens through November 29.
social.long:
Vercel added Tencent’s Hy4 Flash to AI Gateway on November 16, with a separate introductory discount ending November 29. The integration supports structured output and lets developers disable reasoning for requests that do not need it.

For a team testing a cheaper model, the useful unit is an accepted result. A plan with invented deadlines can require repairs even when the first response looks polished. Our proposed test counts those repairs and reviewer minutes alongside the token bill.
social.take: We would compare accepted results at normal rates before moving production traffic. A temporary discount is a good testing window, not a durable budget.
